title: Martin Luther King Jr.: 'Darkness Cannot Drive Out Darkness; Only Light Can Do That'
summary: During the perilous Birmingham campaign in 1963, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. articulated his timeless moral equation: hatred can never defeat hatred; only love can overcome darkness.
keywords: Martin Luther King Jr.: Darkness Cannot Drive Out Darkness
full_text:
In 1963, during the tumultuous civil rights campaigns in Alabama, the home of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was bombed by white supremacists, barely missing his wife Coretta and their infant child. An angry crowd of armed supporters gathered outside, clamoring for violent retaliation.

King stepped onto the shattered porch, held up his hands, and urged the crowd to lay down their weapons. In sermons gathered in his classic work, Strength to Love, King gave immortal expression to the moral philosophy of satyagraha:

"Returning hate for hate multiplies hate, adding deeper darkness to a night already devoid of stars.
Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that.
Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that!
Hate multiplies hate, violence multiplies violence, and toughness multiplies toughness in a descending spiral of destruction. The chain reaction of evil—hate begetting hate, wars producing more wars—must be broken, or we shall be plunged into the dark abyss of annihilation."

King established that non-violent love is not passive surrender, but an active, militant moral power capable of transforming both the oppressor and the oppressed.
